title: Takht Akal Takht
hook: at Amritsar, the timeless throne founded by Guru Hargobind

segments.voice: Yesterday, the five in authority: at Anandpur, at Chamkaur, at a tankhah, at the Akal Takht. Your line was five decide. Which question from your four did you least want to answer? Day one thousand two hundred seventy-nine.

Late at night in Amritsar, after the last hymns, a palanquin is carried out of the Harmandir Sahib, across the causeway, through the courtyard, and up into the building that faces it. Inside rides the Guru Granth Sahib, going to rest for the night. In the early morning it comes back the same way, with singing. So every day the Guru travels between two buildings that look at each other across the courtyard. One stands in the water, low, with doors on every side. The other stands on land, raised, facing it. The Ardas remembers the five Takhts together, and the next days of this path visit them one by one. Today, the one facing the water: Takht Akal Takht.
screen: `A PALANQUIN CROSSES THE COURTYARD.` → `TWO BUILDINGS FACING EACH OTHER.` → `TAKHT AKAL TAKHT.`

segments.voice: Akal means timeless, beyond death; Akal Purakh, the Timeless Being, is a Sikh name for God. Takht means a throne. So the name says the throne of the Timeless. Not the throne of a Guru, not of a ruler. The seat belongs to God, and whoever sits there sits on borrowed ground. Sikh tradition says Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, founded it at Amritsar, facing the Harmandir Sahib, and that he held court there: hearing the sangat, receiving offerings, settling the community's affairs. Tradition adds that the Guru raised the platform with Baba Buddha and Bhai Gurdas, with their own hands. Now the shape of the place, which teaches without words. The Harmandir sits low, in the water, open on all sides. It is where the Guru's word is sung, day and night. The Akal Takht stands on land, raised, looking straight at it. It is where the community's worldly matters are heard. Two buildings, two kinds of work, and neither turned away from the other. The decisions are meant to be made in full view of the hymns. Then the night journey of the Granth closes the loop. The word that is sung in the Harmandir by day rests at the Akal Takht by night. Tradition counts the Akal Takht first among the five Takhts, the one the Guru himself set up, the one from which the edicts this week has talked about go out. The first throne.
screen: `AKAL TAKHT: THE THRONE OF THE TIMELESS.` · `FOUNDED BY GURU HARGOBIND.` · `RAISED, FACING THE HARMANDIR.` · `THE GRANTH RESTS THERE BY NIGHT.` · then, large: `THE FIRST THRONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: picture it facing the Harmandir. Settle, and breathe. See the courtyard at night, the water dark, the lights on the gold doubled underneath. Now turn your back to the water and look up at the Akal Takht, raised, lit, facing you. Then turn round again, toward the Harmandir. Go back and forth slowly, a few times: the place of song, the place of decision. Then let both stand together in your mind, facing each other, and rest there until the bell. The bell holds the time.
Takht Akal Takht. The throne of the Timeless at Amritsar, founded by Guru Hargobind, facing the Harmandir Sahib. Today's word.
Your line: the first throne. Today, before one decision, face the thing you hold most sacred, whatever it is, for a moment, and then decide. Day one thousand two hundred seventy-nine.

howItsDone: At Amritsar the Akal Takht faces the Harmandir Sahib across the courtyard; each night the Guru Granth Sahib is carried there in a palanquin to rest, and returns at dawn.
